items.title: Ask HN: How to deal with shipping AI-written code you don't understand?
items.excerpt: I saw this LinkedIn post from a Meta engineer and it resonated with me:  https://www.linkedin.com/posts/ali-hamie_im-an-engineer-at-m...  > I'm an engineer at Meta and I never felt this uncomfortable doing my job. I'm writing code these days and it all feels like a black box. This new standard of shipping with AI is moving so fast that if we're going to spend our time checking each line of code, it's going to take forever. That means you can end up with systems you've built where you don't truly understand how all the code works. You understand the high level, but not every detail. And maybe t
items.summary: Meta engineer describes difficulty shipping AI-written code without understanding every line, due to speed pressure in shipping with AI-generated systems.
items.usefulness: Could inform decision-making when building Python tools: developers might establish code review gates or testing standards before accepting AI-generated implementations.
items.to_verify: Whether the reported speed-understanding tradeoff applies to specific types of Python code (parsing, document analysis) and what verification methods exist.
